transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah, hey. Um, what brings me in... well, I just can't stop jumping out of my skin lately. Like at work, if a breaker snaps loud, or a tool drops on the concrete, or even if somebody just comes up behind me unannounced, I practically jump out of my boots. And my heart just keeps hammering and hammering long after everyone else has moved on and forgot about it. 

It’s embarrassing, honestly. We were on this big job site over off Route 9 the other day—actually, it was that old strip mall they’re turning into a gym. Have you seen that? They’re putting in one of those fancy places with the indoor rock climbing walls. I don't get the appeal, honestly, paying a hundred bucks a month to climb a fake rock when you could just go outside. My buddy Dave goes to one, but Dave’s always throwing his money away on dumb stuff. He bought a pontoon boat two years ago and it’s just been sitting in his driveway rotting because his wife won't let him take it out on the lake. Needs a new alternator anyway. 

But yeah, anyway, what was I saying? Just... I can't handle the sudden noises anymore. That's why I'm here.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or on edge even when there aren't any sudden noises or surprises around?

I mean, I don't know if I'd say that. I haven't really noticed feeling like that when it's just quiet. Usually if there's no noises, I'm just at home trying to watch TV. Sitting in my recliner. 

It's this old La-Z-Boy I got off Craigslist a few years back. Best fifty bucks I ever spent, honestly. The guy who sold it to me lived way out in the sticks, had this massive German Shepherd that just stared at me the whole time I was loading it into my truck. I drive a '06 Silverado, and the bed is all scratched up from hauling compressor parts and scrap metal, so I didn't care if the chair rubbed against the sides. But man, that dog was huge. I like dogs, though. I had a Beagle when I was a kid, named Buster. He used to dig under the chain-link fence and get into the neighbor's trash. Old Mrs. Higgins would get so mad. She used to make these terrible fruitcakes for Christmas and bring them over, like they were supposed to be a treat or something... I swear they weighed ten pounds. You could use 'em as a doorstop. 

Anyway... sorry, what were you asking? I lost track. Something about being on edge?
Between these loud or sudden noises, do you find yourself constantly scanning your surroundings or feeling like you need to be on guard, even in places you know are safe, like your home?

Scanning? Nah, not really. I don't feel like I gotta be on guard or anything when I'm just sitting at the house. I mean, my house is pretty secure anyway. I put in these new deadbolts a couple months ago. Schlage, heavy duty ones. 

You gotta make sure the strike plate is seated right, though, or the door won't shut flush. I actually had to chisel out the frame on my back door because the wood was all warped from that crazy rain we got last spring. Man, that rain was something else, wasn't it? Flooded out half of Main Street. The storm drains in this town are an absolute joke. City council keeps saying they're gonna fix 'em, but then they go and spend a million bucks on that new fountain downtown by the courthouse. Like anyone cares about a fancy water fountain when their basement's got six inches of muddy water in it. My buddy Rick lost his whole vintage comic book collection to a flood back in 2010. He had them in these cardboard boxes right on the floor. I told him, you gotta put that stuff on pallets, but he didn't listen. 

But, uh... wait, what did you ask me? Something about looking around the house?
Do you find yourself avoiding certain places or situations because you're worried about sudden or loud noises happening there?

Yeah, I guess I do avoid stuff. Like at work, I'll make up all kinds of excuses not to go near certain breaker panels or specific job sites. Or even talk about that day. Because once the thoughts start in my head, I just can't shut them off, you know? It's like a broken record. 

Speaking of records, I found this old box of vinyl in my parents' attic last weekend. Some really good stuff in there—Zeppelin, Sabbath, some early Aerosmith. My dad had this old turntable, a Technics, I think. Heavy as a brick. He used to play it on Sunday mornings while my mom was making pancakes. She always burned the first batch, every single time. Said the pan had to "warm up," but I think she just got distracted watching the birds out the kitchen window. We had these blue jays that would fight over the feeder. Mean little birds, blue jays. They'd chase off all the cardinals and the chickadees. I tried putting out sunflower seeds to see if that would calm them down, but they just got more aggressive. Kind of like this guy I used to work with, Gary. Give him an inch, he'd take a mile. He borrowed my socket set once and returned it missing the 10-millimeter. It's always the 10-millimeter, right? You can never find those things when you need them. I swear there's a black hole somewhere just full of 10-millimeter sockets and left socks. 

But, uh... what was I saying? Something about work?
Have you noticed that these reactions to loud noises bring back memories or feelings from a particular moment or event that was really upsetting or traumatic for you?

Yeah, I mean... yeah. It does. Out of nowhere I'll just see that flash in my head, or I'll hear the trainee yelling. It doesn't even have to be a loud noise that sets it off, honestly. I could just be loading tools into the back of the truck, minding my own business, and it just knocks me sideways like it's happening all over again. 

I keep all my tools in this big diamond-plate Weather Guard box. Best investment I ever made for that truck. The cheap plastic ones just crack in the winter when it gets below freezing. I had a buddy, Steve, who bought one of those plastic ones from a discount auto place, and the first time it dropped below twenty degrees, he slammed the lid and the whole corner just shattered off. He was so mad. Tried to tape it up with duct tape, but you know how that goes once the moisture gets in there. The tape just peels right off. Plus, the adhesive gets all gummy and ruins whatever you set on it. I tried using Goo Gone to get some old sticker residue off my bumper once, and it completely stripped the clear coat. Had to take it to this body shop out on Highway 9. The guy running the place, big fella named Earl, he had this old vintage gas pump right in the middle of his waiting room. Restored it himself, painted it bright red. Said he found it in a barn out in Nebraska. I always wanted to do a road trip out west, maybe see the Badlands or Mount Rushmore. I hear it's a lot of driving with nothing to look at but cornfields, though. 

But... wait. What were we talking about? Something about the truck?
